provenance.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
affiliations: Department of Computer Science, Princeton University
provenance.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance across tasks in language understanding and interactive decision making, their abilities for reasoning and acting have primarily been studied as separate topics. We explore the use of LLMs to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, allowing for greater synergy: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans and handle exceptions, while actions allow it to interface with external sources such as knowledge bases or environments. Applied to HotpotQA, Fever, ALFWorld, and WebShop, ReAct outperforms baselines with improved interpretability and trustworthiness.
key_claims: Interleaving reasoning traces ('thoughts') with task-specific actions produces synergy: reasoning helps guide/track/repair action plans, and actions ground reasoning in external information.
ReAct overcomes hallucination and error-propagation issues of chain-of-thought (CoT) on HotpotQA and FEVER by interacting with a Wikipedia API, while remaining competitive with CoT.
On ALFWorld and Webshop, ReAct outperforms imitation/RL baselines by absolute success-rate gains of 34% and 10% respectively using only 1-2 in-context examples.
Combining ReAct with CoT-Self-Consistency (switching heuristically between the two) outperforms either method alone.
ReAct trajectories are more human-interpretable and allow human-in-the-loop correction by editing 'thoughts' rather than model parameters or full action sequences.

architecture.primary_variant: ReAct (Reason + Act) prompting loop over a frozen LLM

modules.name: Frozen Policy LLM
modules.input_shape: context sequence c_t = (o_1, a_1, ..., o_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, o_t) as tokenized text
modules.output_shape: next augmented action a_hat_t (text token sequence representing either a 'thought' or a domain action)

parameters.prompting_mode: few-shot in-context learning, 1-6 exemplars, no gradient updates in main experiments

modules.notes: The 'model' is not a novel neural architecture; ReAct is a prompting/decoding paradigm applied to an existing frozen LLM. Finetuning experiments in Section 3.3/Appendix B.1 use PaLM-8B/62B decoders trained to emit trajectories, but no new architecture is introduced.

modules.name: Thought Generator (Reasoning Trace Emitter)
modules.operation_type: language_generation_step (aihat_t in L, no environment effect)
modules.output_shape: free-form natural language thought aihat_t, appended to context as c_{t+1} = (c_t, aihat_t)

purpose_categories: track progress and transition between subgoals
handle exceptions and reformulate a plan

modules.notes: Thoughts occupy an unbounded language space L and produce no observation/environment feedback; they only update the context for future reasoning/acting.

modules.name: Action Executor
modules.input_shape: action string a_t in A (domain-specific), parsed from LLM output
modules.output_shape: observation o_{t+1} returned by the environment/API

parameters.action_space_ALFWorld: environment-defined text actions, e.g. go to X, open X, take X from Y, clean X with Y, put X in/on Y
action_space_WebShop: think[...] (treated as a thought, not an action)

modules.notes: For HotpotQA/FEVER this is a custom simplified Wikipedia API (search returns first 5 sentences of an entity page or 5 similar entity suggestions; lookup simulates Ctrl+F). For ALFWorld/WebShop the action interface is the benchmark's native text-action environment.

modules.name: Wikipedia Web API
modules.output_shape: first 5 sentences of an entity page, OR top-5 similar entity names, OR next sentence containing the lookup string

parameters.search: returns first 5 sentences of corresponding entity wiki page if it exists, else top-5 similar entities from Wikipedia search engine
parameters.lookup: returns the next sentence in the page containing the given string (simulates browser Ctrl+F)
parameters.finish: terminates the episode with a final answer

modules.notes: Deliberately weaker than SOTA neural/lexical retrievers; designed to force explicit reasoning-driven retrieval rather than powerful retrieval doing the work.

modules.name: Context Aggregator / Working Memory
modules.input_shape: prior context c_t plus new thought or (action, observation) pair
modules.notes: c_t = (o_1, a_1, ..., o_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, o_t) is simply the concatenated trajectory fed back into the LLM prompt each step; there is no separate learned memory module.

modules.name: CoT-SC Fallback Module
modules.output_shape: majority-vote answer over n=21 sampled CoT trajectories (temperature 0.7)

parameters.switch_heuristic_ReAct_to_CoTSC: back off to CoT-SC if ReAct fails to finish within 7 steps (HotpotQA) or 5 steps (FEVER)
parameters.switch_heuristic_CoTSC_to_ReAct: back off to ReAct if the majority answer among n CoT-SC samples occurs less than n/2 times

modules.notes: This is a separate baseline/ensemble method combined with ReAct via hand-designed heuristics, not part of the core ReAct loop itself.

differences.thought_frequency: thoughts appear only sparsely at the most relevant positions, LLM decides occurrence

differences.removes: all 'thought'/aihat_t steps, keeps only actions and observations
all actions and observations, reasoning-only chain-of-thought

differences.adds: 21 sampled CoT trajectories at temperature 0.7 with majority vote

differences.removes: all thoughts, actions, and observations; direct answer prompting

differences.restricts: thoughts limited to (1) decomposing current goal and (2) current subgoal only; lacks subgoal-completion detection, next-subgoal determination, and commonsense-location reasoning

mathematical_spec.name: Policy over augmented action space
mathematical_spec.latex: a_t \sim \pi(a_t \mid c_t), \quad c_t = (o_1, a_1, \ldots, o_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, o_t)

mathematical_spec.name: Context update rule after a thought
WebShop task score (attribute coverage)
undefined_symbols: coverage(\cdot,\cdot) exact functional form not given in main text

tensor_semantics.name: o_t
tensor_semantics.shape_notation: variable-length text token sequence (environment observation at time t)

tensor_semantics.name: a_t
tensor_semantics.shape_notation: variable-length text token sequence (domain action drawn from A)

tensor_semantics.name: a_hat_t (thought)
tensor_semantics.shape_notation: variable-length text token sequence drawn from language space L

tensor_semantics.name: c_t (context)
tensor_semantics.shape_notation: concatenation of (o_1, a_1, ..., o_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, o_t), length grows with t, truncated to LLM context window

training_pipeline.notes: The paper's MAIN experiments (Sections 3-4, Tables 1/3/4) use pure few-shot in-context prompting with a frozen LLM -- there is no training loop, optimizer, or learning rate for these results. A secondary finetuning experiment (Appendix B.1, referenced in Section 3.3 'Finetuning') bootstraps 3,000 ReAct-generated trajectories to finetune smaller PaLM-8B/62B decoder models with batch size 64; ReAct/Act are trained for 4,000 steps and Standard/CoT for 2,000 steps (PaLM-8B) or 1,000 steps (PaLM-62B). No optimizer name, learning rate, or schedule is given in the visible text for this finetuning stage.

evaluation_protocol.compute: PaLM-540B, PaLM-8B, PaLM-62B (Google's Pathways LM); GPT-3 text-davinci-002 for auxiliary experiments (Appendix A.1). No specific GPU/TPU count or wall-clock time is stated in the visible text.
special_conditions: Greedy decoding used for all main prompting results
BUTLER baseline uses beam search (best of 8)
ReAct/Act ALFWorld results reported as best-of-6 and average-of-6 across prompt permutations
CoT-SC uses 21 sampled trajectories at temperature 0.7

implementation_assumptions.assumption: PaLM-540B is not publicly accessible, so a faithful reproduction must substitute an accessible LLM (e.g. GPT-3/GPT-4 class or open-weight model) via API, matching the paper's own GPT-3 ablation methodology (Appendix A.1).
alternatives: Use GPT-3 text-davinci-002 as in Appendix A.1
Use a modern open-weight LLM (e.g. Llama-family) with few-shot ReAct prompts

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Exact wording and full text of the in-context exemplar prompts (6 for HotpotQA, 3 for FEVER, 3-per-task-type x6 permutations for ALFWorld) are in Appendix C, which is not included in the parsed text; must be reconstructed from the illustrative examples shown in Figure 1 and Tables 6-9.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from context; Appendix C referenced but its full contents not present in parsed document
alternatives: Hand-author new exemplars following the documented thought-type taxonomy

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Wikipedia API backing search/lookup/finish must be implemented as a lightweight wrapper (e.g. Wikipedia REST API or `wikipedia` Python package) rather than a full neural retriever, to match the paper's intentionally weak retrieval design.
implementation_assumptions.basis: common practice / explicit design rationale in Section 3.1
alternatives: Use the Wikipedia API python package
Use a static dump indexed with a simple keyword lookup

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Decoding temperature for all main ReAct/Act/CoT prompting results is 0 (greedy), since only CoT-SC explicitly states temperature 0.7.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from context (Section 3.2 Baselines paragraph, and GPT-3 experiments stating 'greedy decoding')
alternatives: Some small nonzero temperature with fixed seed

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Finetuning experiments (Appendix B.1) use a standard cross-entropy next-token objective with Adam-family optimizer, since PaLM finetuning defaults are not restated in this paper.
implementation_assumptions.basis: literature default for PaLM finetuning (Chowdhery et al. 2022)
alternatives: Adafactor optimizer as used in original PaLM training

implementation_assumptions.assumption: The ALFWorld/WebShop 'observation' text format (e.g. object lists, room descriptions) follows the benchmark's default environment renderer, not a paper-specific custom format.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from context; consistent with cited Shridhar et al. 2020b and Yao et al. 2022 benchmark papers

implementation_assumptions.assumption: The number of in-context steps allowed before backing off from ReAct to CoT-SC (7 for HotpotQA, 5 for FEVER) is a hard step cap on the Thought-Action-Observation loop, not a token limit.

ambiguities.description: search[entity] is stated to return 'the first 5 sentences from the corresponding entity wiki page if it exists, or else suggests top-5 similar entities' -- exact sentence-segmentation and similarity-ranking algorithm for the 'suggests similar entities' fallback is not specified.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Use the native Wikipedia search-suggest API for the fallback and a standard sentence tokenizer (e.g. nltk/spacy) for the 5-sentence extraction.
alternatives: Use of a TF-IDF/BM25 ranked candidate list

ambiguities.location: Section 4, 'For robustness, we construct 6 prompts for each task type through each permutation of 2 annotated trajectories from the 3 we annotate'
ambiguities.description: Exact identities of the 3 annotated ALFWorld trajectories per task type (6 task types) are not included in the parsed text (would be in Appendix C.4).
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Author-authored trajectories following the four documented thought categories (decompose goal, track subgoal completion, determine next subgoal, commonsense reasoning about object location).
alternatives: Reconstruct from the official released code repository (react-lm.github.io)

ambiguities.description: The 'average score' metric's precise computation (how partial attribute coverage is weighted/normalized per episode) is only described at a high level ('percentage of desired attributes covered by the chosen product averaged across all episodes').
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Score_i = (# matched attributes for chosen product) / (# requested attributes in instruction), averaged over the 500 test instructions.
alternatives: Weighted attribute importance scheme from original WebShop paper (Yao et al. 2022) rather than uniform averaging

ambiguities.description: The human-labeling protocol for classifying 50+50 sampled HotpotQA trajectories into 'reasoning error', 'search result error', 'hallucination', and 'label ambiguity' categories is described narratively but the annotation guidelines/inter-rater agreement are not given.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Single-annotator (author) manual labeling without a formal codebook; not reproducible as a precise algorithm.
